title: Plain-language explainer: what a reproducible reanalysis does/does not show (education only)
context: M4 is a strictly optional, opt-in track. The core project ships without it. If pursued, this explainer is education-only content for patient advocates and the interested public: it explains what a reproducible reanalysis does and does not show, without any diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment guidance. Every claim must be sourced and provenanced. Release is blocked until a credentialed oncologist AND a patient advocate both sign off — this is a non-skippable dual gate. This task should not begin until M3 is complete and both reviewers are confirmed.
objective: Write a plain-language explainer for patient advocates and the interested public describing what a reproducible cancer-proteomics reanalysis does and does not show, framed as education only with a prominent 'not medical advice' notice and sourced claims.
acceptanceCriteria: The explainer is education-only content: it describes what reproducible reanalysis means, why it matters for research trust, and what limits it has — with no diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment guidance and no patient-specific interpretation.
A prominent 'not medical advice' notice appears on the document; every factual claim is sourced and provenanced.

Blocking dual sign-off: a credentialed oncologist AND a patient advocate both review and approve the explainer before any release; sign-off evidence (name, credentials, date) is recorded and committed.
No release of any version of this document without both sign-offs recorded; if either reviewer is not secured, the document is held and the blocker is surfaced.
The explainer is licensed CC-BY-4.0; verifiedNeed is set to true only once an advocate or educator formally requests it.
